ukmt-maclaurin-2016-m2.title: Count area and perimeter in terms of the number of rows
ukmt-maclaurin-2016-m2.body:
Let there be $n$ rows. The rows have $1,3,5,\dots,2n-1$ squares from the top.

Area: $A=1+3+\cdots+(2n-1)=n^2$ (sum of the first $n$ odd numbers; or rearrange the shape into an $n\times n$ square by cutting it in two pieces and turning one over).

Perimeter: look at the shape from the left and from the right: each row contributes one vertical unit edge on each side, giving $n+n=2n$ in total on the left and right. Viewed from above, the horizontal edges project onto the bottom row of width $2n-1$, giving $2n-1$ horizontal units on top; likewise $2n-1$ below (the shape's underside is the bottom row). So $P=2n+(2n-1)+(2n-1)=6n-2$.

Then $(P+2)^2=(6n)^2=36n^2=36A$. ∎

ukmt-maclaurin-2016-m3.title: Coordinates
ukmt-maclaurin-2016-m3.body:
Let the squares with centres $A,B,C$ have sides $2a,2b,2c$. The squares at $A$ and $B$ are stacked on the right, and their total height $2a+2b$ equals the side $2c$ of the big square, so $c=a+b$.

Put $O$ at the origin with the $x$-axis along the bottom edges and the $y$-axis along the vertical line through $O$. Then the big square occupies $-2c\le x\le0$, $0\le y\le2c$; square $A$ occupies $0\le x\le2a$, $0\le y\le2a$; square $B$ occupies $0\le x\le2b$, $2a\le y\le 2a+2b$. The centres are
$$A=(a,a),\quad B=(b,2a+b),\quad C=(-c,c)=(-a-b,a+b).$$
Hence $\vec{OB}=(b,\,2a+b)$ and $\vec{AC}=C-A=(-2a-b,\,b)$.

The vector $\vec{AC}$ is $\vec{OB}$ rotated through $90^\circ$ anticlockwise: $(x,y)\mapsto(-y,x)$ takes $(b,2a+b)$ to $(-2a-b,b)$. A rotation by $90^\circ$ preserves length and turns a vector into a perpendicular one, so $OB=AC$ and $OB\perp AC$. ∎

ukmt-maclaurin-2016-m4.title: Factorise
ukmt-maclaurin-2016-m4.body:
$3x^2+xy-2y^2=(3x-2y)(x+y)=-5$ and $(x+y)^2=1$. So $x+y=\pm1$.

- $x+y=1$: $3x-2y=-5$. Then $5x=-5+2=-3$, so $x=-\tfrac35$ and $y=\tfrac85$.
- $x+y=-1$: $3x-2y=5$. Then $5x=5-2=3$, so $x=\tfrac35$, $y=-\tfrac85$.

Both satisfy the original equations (each is obtained by reversible steps).

**Answer: $(x,y)=(\tfrac35,-\tfrac85)$ and $(-\tfrac35,\tfrac85)$**

ukmt-maclaurin-2016-m4.title: Combine the equations
ukmt-maclaurin-2016-m4.body: Add the first equation to $5\times$ the second: $8x^2+11xy+3y^2=0$, i.e. $(8x+3y)(x+y)=0$. If $x+y=0$ the second equation reads $0=1$, impossible. So $8x+3y=0$, $y=-\tfrac{8x}3$; the second equation gives $25x^2/9=1$, $x=\pm\tfrac35$, giving the same two solutions.

ukmt-maclaurin-2016-m5.title: Rearrange and compare signs
ukmt-maclaurin-2016-m5.body:
Let the room number be $\overline{abc}=100a+10b+c$ with $a\ge1$. Suppose $100a+10b+c=(a+1)(b+1)c$. Then
$$100a+10b+c-a(b+1)c-(b+1)c=0\iff(100-(b+1)c)\,a+(10-c)\,b=0.$$
Now $(b+1)c\le10\cdot9=90$, so $100-(b+1)c\ge10>0$ and, as $a\ge1$, the first term is at least $10$. Also $10-c\ge1$ and $b\ge0$, so the second term is $\ge0$. The left side is therefore positive, contradicting the equation. So I was mistaken. ∎
